# `scikitplot`

<!-- Generated by `python tools/maint_tools/generate_usage_skills.py sync` from the installed package; edit the module's docstrings or `__all__`, not this file. -->

An intuitive library that seamlessly adds plotting capabilities and functionality to any model objects or outputs, compatible with tools like scikit-learn, XGBoost, TensorFlow, and more.

## Install

```sh
pip install scikit-plots
```

The release on PyPI can be older than the version this skill was read from; a
name below can be missing from it. The [release history on
PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/scikit-plots/#history) lists each release, and
[pip's user guide](https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/user_guide/) explains
upgrading.

## Before writing code

The API below was read from one version of the package. Check the version the
project has, and read a name's docstring and signature before calling it:

```sh
python -c "import scikitplot; print(scikitplot.__version__)"
python -c "import scikitplot as m, inspect; print(inspect.signature(m.<name>)); help(m.<name>)"
```

## Public API

Declared in `scikitplot.__all__`, in that order.

| Name | Kind | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| `LowLevelCallable` | class | Low-level callback function. |
| `annotations` | _Feature |  |
| `citation` | function | Return a BibTeX citation of scikit-plots. |
| `config_context` | function | Context manager for global scikit-plots configuration. |
| `get_config` | function | Retrieve current values for configuration set by `set_config`. |
| `get_logger` | function | Return SP (scikitplot) logger instance. |
| `online_help` | function | Open the online documentation search page in the default web browser. |
| `set_config` | function | Set global scikit-plots configuration. |
| `show_config` | function | Show libraries and system information on which SciPy was built and is being used |
| `show_versions` | function | Print or return debugging information about the system, Python, dependencies, and hardware. |
| `test` | PytestTester |  |

All names with signatures: [references/API.md](references/API.md).

## Example (from the docstring of `scikitplot.citation`)

```pycon
>>> from scikitplot.config import citation
>>> citation() == citation("all")
True
>>> citation("build").startswith("@software{scikit-plots_v")
True
```
